summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis with hyperglycemia, abdominal pain, and purulent drainage from her GJ tube site. She was stabilized in the ICU with an insulin drip and IV fluids, resolving her DKA. During the hospitalization, the external portion of her GJ tube was found disconnected, and a fractured segment was retained in the stomach. She underwent a successful radiologically guided procedure to remove the fragment and replace the GJ tube. She improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with updated insulin therapy, pain medication supply for her scheduled pain clinic visit, and instructions for tube site care. Her mental health and compliance were supported throughout by her medical guardian.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Mechanical complication of colostomy and enterostomy
Attention to other artificial opening of digestive tract
